system.name: BoS
system.one_liner: an in-network data plane that runs NN-driven (binary RNN + escalation to a transformer) traffic analysis at line-speed

content.subject: comparing two ways to implement RNN time steps on a switch: storing hidden states versus storing embedding vectors

elements.name: h_t
elements.role: the GRU cell's hidden-state output at the current time step

elements.name: GRU
elements.role: the recurrent cell computing the new hidden state from the input event and its own previous output via a self-loop

elements.name: ev_t
elements.role: the input event/embedding fed to the GRU at the current time step

relations.what: self-loop: the hidden state feeds back as the cell's own recurrent input

panels.label: (a) RNN cell
panels.differs: the baseline template: one GRU cell with a self-loop turning its own output h_t back into a recurrent input

panels.label: (b) solution 1
panels.differs: unrolls the self-loop across pipeline stages in time and keeps the hidden state (h_{t-1}, h_t) in switch storage (yellow highlight), reading and writing it as each new event ev_t arrives

panels.label: (c) solution 2
panels.differs: instead keeps the sequence of input events (ev_1...ev_t) in switch storage (yellow highlight) and re-runs the full chain of GRU cells across serial stages for every new packet

content.key_idea: Because a switch register can only be read/written once per packet, BoS cannot keep a GRU cell's self-loop; it must unroll RNN time steps across pipeline stages, storing either the running hidden state (solution 1) or the input embeddings (solution 2).
content.reading_order: left to right across the three panels: (a) the plain single-cell RNN template, (b) solution 1's hidden-state storage with the highlight on h_{t-1}/h_t, and (c) solution 2's embedding storage spanning ev_1 through ev_t.

summary: Figure 3 compares two ways BoS can unroll RNN time steps onto a switch pipeline, starting from the plain RNN cell template in (a): one GRU box that feeds its own hidden-state output h_t back into itself as a recurrent input. Because a switch register can be read and written only once per packet, that self-loop cannot survive as drawn, so (b) 'solution 1' spreads the loop across pipeline stages by storing the running hidden state (h_{t-1}, h_t, shown inside a yellow 'switch storage' halo) and re-injecting it at each new event ev_t, while surrounding, not-currently-active time steps are greyed out. Alternative (c) 'solution 2' instead keeps the whole sequence of input embeddings ev_1...ev_t in switch storage and re-executes the full chain of GRU cells in serial stages for every new packet. BoS adopts solution 2 in its final prototype because it uses fewer hardware resources.
summary_zh: 图3对比BoS展开RNN时间步的两种方案：(a)原始GRU单元自环；(b)方案一将隐藏状态存入交换机存储并跨流水线级读写；(c)方案二改存嵌入向量序列，最终因硬件开销更小被采用。
